content: Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by altering the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of brigatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is necessary, and close monitoring is required. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by approximately 50% without breaking tablets (e.g., from 180 mg to 90 mg or from 90 mg to 60 mg). After discontinuing mifepristone, resume the previously tolerated brigatinib dose. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of bromocriptine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone is contraindicated with budesonide due to an unknown mechanism. The manufacturer states that mifepristone is contraindicated in patients receiving budesonide. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of buprenorphine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of buprenorphine buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, or long-acting injection formulations, and all combinations increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of bupropion by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of buspirone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Start with 5 mg orally twice daily and adjust the dose based on clinical response. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of cabozantinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. For patients taking cabozantinib tablets, reduce the dose by 20 mg (e.g., from 60 mg/day to 40 mg/day or from 40 mg/day to 20 mg/day). For patients taking cabozantinib capsules, reduce the dose by 40 mg (e.g., from 140 mg/day to 100 mg/day or from 100 mg/day to 60 mg/day). Resume the previous cabozantinib dose 2–3 days after discontinuing mifepristone. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of calcifediol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of calcitriol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of cannabidiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of capivasertib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of capmatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of carbamazepine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, carbamazepine can decrease the levels or effects of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of cariprazine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cenobamate can decrease the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Increase the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. Mifepristone increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs can increase each other's toxicity by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Additionally, both drugs increase the QTc interval, and co-administration should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Chloramphenicol can increase the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of chloroquine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Chloroquine can also increase mifepristone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring is recommended. Mifepristone can increase the toxicity of cholic acid by decreasing its elimination. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Avoid concomitant use of bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) inhibitors, as this may exacerbate the accumulation of conjugated bile salts in the liver, leading to clinical symptoms. If co-administration is necessary, monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin levels. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of ciclesonide inhaled by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of cilostazol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ciprofloxacin can increase the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Use alternatives if available. Mifepristone is contraindicated with cisapride due to the risk of QTc interval prolongation. Both drugs can increase each other's levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of citalopram by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If concurrent therapy is essential, ECG monitoring is recommended. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. The combination may also prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of clomipramine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Use alternatives if available. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of clonazepam by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of clozapine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Use alternatives if available. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If co-administration is necessary, adjust the mifepristone dose based on the patient's current regimen. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of cobimetinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. For short-term co-administration (14 days or less), reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg once daily for patients normally taking 60 mg daily. After discontinuing mifepristone, resume the previous cobimetinib dose. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of colchicine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of colchicine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of conivaptan by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of copanlisib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone is contraindicated with cortisone due to an unknown mechanism. The manufacturer states that mifepristone is contraindicated in patients on long-term corticosteroid therapy. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of crizotinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide by altering CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Cyclophosphamide can also increase mifepristone levels. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Mifepristone can increase the levels of cyclosporine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the narrow therapeutic index of cyclosporine. Mifepristone is contraindicated with dabigatran due to the risk of excessive post-abortion bleeding in patients on anticoagulant therapy. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of dabrafenib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of daclatasvir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone is contraindicated with dalteparin due to the risk of excessive post-abortion bleeding in patients on anticoagulant therapy. Danazol can increase the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of daprodustat by altering CYP2C8 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the daprodustat starting dose by half when co-administered with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of dapsone by inhibiting CYP2C8/2C9. Use the smallest recommended doses for substrates and monitor closely. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of daridorexant by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of darifenacin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Darunavir can increase the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of dasatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
